170	# Resolve USART3 RS485 and ST-LINK VCP conflict
171	
172	## Goal
173	
174	Move the VelaGuard RS485 transport to an electrically independent UART while
175	preserving the proven ST-LINK VCP console and SWD workflow. Deliver the board
176	and configuration foundation, wiring guidance, and a deterministic raw
177	bidirectional smoke test needed before later Modbus integration.
178	
179	## Background and Confirmed Facts
180	
181	- The target is an STM32H750B-DK, board revision MB1381 B01.
182	- On MB1381 B01, USART3 PB10/PB11 is shared by Arduino D1/D0 and ST-LINK VCP.
183	  R184 carries target PB10 to ST-LINK RX; R188 carries ST-LINK TX to target
184	  PB11. The existing MAX485ESA adapter also uses PB10/PB11, so its original
185	  wiring creates a real electrical and traffic-ownership conflict.
186	- The current firmware uses USART3 at 115200 8N1 for the serial console, NSH,
187	  startup output, and syslog. This working COM7 development/recovery path must
188	  remain unchanged.
189	- The accepted allocation moves RS485 to UART7 and leaves USART3, R184, and
190	  R188 untouched. UART7 TX is PB4/Arduino D10, UART7 RX is PA8/Arduino D5, and
191	  the direction signal is PK1/Arduino D4.
192	- PB4, PA8, and PK1 are 5 V-tolerant according to STM32H750XB DS12556. PB4 is
193	  also NJTRST, but the project's SWD-only path uses PA13/PA14 and does not
194	  require NJTRST.
195	- The original automatic-direction MAX485ESA module will be replaced with a
196	  3.3 V RS485 transceiver exposing DI, RO, DE, and active-low RE. DE and
197	  active-low RE will be tied together and driven by PK1; high selects transmit
198	  and low selects receive.
199	- The current STM32H7 serial driver supports `CONFIG_UART7_RS485` and requires
200	  the board to define `GPIO_UART7_RS485_DIR`. It rejects UART RXDMA or TXDMA
201	  combined with RS485, so UART7 DMA must remain disabled.
202	- No real Modbus sensor or PC-side USB-RS485 adapter is currently available.
203	  Procurement is approved for the 3.3 V transceiver, a USB-RS485 adapter,
204	  wiring, and 120-ohm termination.
205	- The existing NuttX `serialrx` and `serialblaster` applications are sufficient
206	  for the board side of a deterministic raw-link test. A Windows PowerShell
207	  peer script will send and verify the matching byte sequences over the
208	  PC-side USB-RS485 COM port.
209	- The existing QSPI patch is already applied in the working NuttX checkout.
210	  UART7 RS485 support must use a separate idempotent patch so QSPI patch
211	  detection is not broken by partially applied combined content.

218	  and PK1/D4 as the active-high transmit direction output.
219	- Use a 3.3 V manual-direction RS485 transceiver with DE and active-low RE tied
220	  together. PK1 must initialize low so the transceiver starts in receive mode.
221	- Enable UART7 serial and RS485 support at 9600 8N1 with both UART7 DMA paths
